title: Stacks & Queues
summary: Stacks and queues control the order data is processed. A stack is last in, first out (like undo or a pile of plates); a queue is first in, first out (like a line at a coffee shop). The lesson builds both as Python classes with add, remove and peek methods. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Build a Stack and a Queue class in Python and pick the right one for a problem.

steps.title: Read the lesson
steps.detail: Read the Stacks and Queues page, including the addTop/removeTop/peek and addRight/removeLeft/peek methods.
steps.doneWhen: You can give one real-world example of a stack and one of a queue.

steps.title: Run the curriculum's Stack and Queue
steps.detail: Save and run this condensed version of the lesson's classes.
steps.doneWhen: It prints 3 (the newest) for the stack and 1 (the oldest) for the queue.

steps.title: Spot the hidden cost
steps.detail: list.pop(0) moves every other item over, so it is O(n). Python's collections.deque has popleft(), which is O(1). Rewrite the Queue with deque and keep the same method names.
steps.doneWhen: Your deque version prints the same output as before.

steps.title: Talk through Valid Parentheses first
steps.detail: Valid Parentheses is one of this lesson's assignments and a classic interview question. Before coding, say the approach out loud (push openers, pop and match on closers, stack must be empty at the end) and its Big-O (time O(n), space O(n)).
steps.doneWhen: You can explain the approach and its Big-O without looking at code.

concepts.meaning: Last in, first out: the newest item is removed first.
First in, first out: the oldest item is removed first.
Add to and remove from the top of a stack.
Look at the next item without removing it.
Python's double-ended queue; adding or removing at either end is O(1).
